mtr.title: Mid-Term Review of the National Cashew Policy 2022–2027
goalProgress: A. Goal 1 – Production. In 2025, total output reached 964,700 tons, up 89.80 percent from 508,283 tons in 2022. Cultivation and crop-management practices improved, especially through the planting of the high-yielding M23 variety, which raised yields to 1.52 tons per hectare. This variety also produces larger nuts with good taste and higher nutritional value. Alongside this major progress, Cambodia is also pursuing priority measures such as climate-resilient production practices, improved farmer awareness of drying and storage, and farmer mobilizing into cooperatives.

B. Goal 2 – Domestic processing. Processing 22,600 tons of cashew generated about 6,300 tons of processed kernels; an increase of 13 percent compared with the 20,000 tons recorded in 2021. Factories and enterprises have an annual processing capacity of about 86,800 tons, but actual processing has reached only 26 percent of that capacity. Progress toward the target of 25 percent domestic processing by 2027 continues to face major constraints, especially the shortage of working capital. Nevertheless, stakeholders remain highly optimistic about investment in the processing industry, as reflected in the growing number of processing enterprises and the strong interest shown by major foreign investors, which could contribute to Cambodia’s industrialization in the future. The development of the Cashew Industrial Park in Kampong Thom (CIP) and the approval of Qualified Investment Projects (QIPs) will be important drivers for the cashew sector.

C. Goal 3 - Exports and market diversification. Farmers continue to export raw cashew nuts, mainly to neighboring country. In 2025, Cambodia exported around 971,000 tons to international markets, of which more than 90 percent went to Viet Nam. Efforts to diversify markets remain active, even though domestic processing volumes are still limited.

criteria.Relevance: The goals and policy actions of the National Cashew Policy remain closely aligned with the current needs of farmers, processors and exporters in Cambodia. The 44 actions identified during policy formulation in 2022 continue to be appropriate measures for addressing the sector’s present challenges. Accelerating implementation of these actions therefore remains a necessary priority. The policy’s vision and objectives also remain well suited to addressing both the constraints and the opportunities facing the cashew sector in the current context, particularly the Royal Government’s ambition to transform Cambodia into one of the world’s leading cashew exporters and a future “Cashew Emperor”.
criteria.Coherence: The National Cashew Policy has shown strong coherence with development partner projects as well as private-sector initiatives. Many development projects currently being implemented in Cambodia contain strategies or activities that are consistent with those set out in the policy, even where those projects cover multiple products or are cross-sectoral in nature. Their activities include climate-resilient production techniques, farmer organization and support to agricultural cooperatives, solutions for drying and warehouse storage, support to domestic processors, and international market linkages. The private sector has likewise undertaken activities aligned with the policy’s strategy, including investments that increase domestic value addition, technical capacity building to strengthen competitiveness, and market strategies consistent with the Royal Government’s export direction.
criteria.Effectiveness: The policy implementation plan is organized into three action clusters covering 44 actions. As of mid-2025, overall implementation progress is generally good: 15 actions (34.09 percent) were fully achieved, 23 actions (52.27 percent) were largely achieved, and 6 actions (13.63 percent) remained limited.
criteria.Efficiency: The policy has made highly efficient use of available resources. Ministries and institutions have shown creative capacity to use national budgets and the resources already available within their respective institutions, while also mobilizing support from development partner projects to implement activities, thereby saving both time and public resources. The mid-term review found, however, that progress toward Goal 2 could be further improved if timely solutions are put in place for processors’ working-capital constraints and if investment-promotion measures are accelerated through the Cashew Industrial Park in Kampong Thom (CIP) and the approval of Qualified Investment Projects (QIPs) for the cashew sector.
criteria.Impact: The economic impacts arising from the implementation of the policy have been reflected in the expansion of cashew production and export earnings. In 2025, the estimated cash flow generated within Cambodia’s economy amounted to approximately USD 1.3 billion, most of which accrued as income to more than 200,000 farming households. This result shows that cashew is not only a crop that can improve people’s livelihoods, but also a strategic crop that has contributed to promoting and creating opportunities for women to participate in cashew cultivation at about 43 percent and in processing activities at between 66 percent and 90 percent. Achieving the policy’s three goals will increase employment in the agro-industrial sector and help build Cambodia’s reputation in international markets.
criteria.Sustainability: Sustainability of the cashew sector is not yet firm, owing to high risks related to markets and the domestic processing base. Dependence on a single market and on exports of unprocessed raw material leaves Cambodia vulnerable when international prices fluctuate or when import policies change. In addition, the high cost of agricultural inputs contributes to cashew price volatility and can negatively affect farmer income and the sustainability of the sector as a whole. On the processing side, producers continue to face many constraints, together with higher production costs than Cambodia’s competitors, making processors more vulnerable. In terms of environmental sustainability, there is still no sign that cashew farmers are using chemicals at levels that pose serious danger, but control measures should continue to be strengthened and monitored. In terms of institutional sustainability, the MTR team observed that organizing farmers into groups, cooperatives, associations and a cashew federation is a sustainable strategic approach.

priorities: To achieve the three policy goals by 2027, especially the target of 25 percent domestic processing, the relevant ministries and institutions should prioritize the following actions:

A. Operationalize the Cashew Industrial Park (CIP) in Kampong Thom Province as planned so that it can provide adequate infrastructure for the clustered development of cashew processing activities and cashew by-product industries and provide incentives through Qualified Investment Project (QIP) schemes to attract large investors.

B. Address the financing shortage facing domestic processors so that they can purchase, store and process raw cashew nuts. Support relevant stakeholders to provide credit products suited to the agro-industrial context. Appropriate financial products could include overdraft facilities or credit lines for the cashew value chain, provided by policy banks or commercial banks, potentially with guarantees from the Credit Guarantee Corporation of Cambodia (CGCC). These credit products should function as working capital for processors, linked to actual purchase orders and flexible in collateral requirements, or without requiring immovable property as security.

C. Support stakeholders in identifying solutions to reduce electricity costs for the agro-industrial sector, streamline export procedures through digital platforms in order to save time and costs for exporters, and support processors through improved production technology, skills development, incentives for product diversification, and greater use of cashew by-products.
D. Prepare clear market strategies focused on destinations such as the European Union, the United States, China and ASEAN.

Production: To preserve the sector’s strengths and resilience, stakeholders should continue a number of priority activities:
Conduct rigorous research on new varieties including M7, M1, SAN1, F40 and P2 and assess possibility for registration as national varieties.
Compile scientific findings on widely used varieties such as M23 and H09, and prepare guidance on climate-resilient production measures.
Compile data on cashew nursery and grafting operators, and provide technical training on varietal management to support long-term crop management.
Train farmers in selected target areas on drying and post-harvest storage to move current practices away from the sale of fresh raw nuts without value addition and with high exposure to market risk.

Assess the capacity of farmer cooperatives nationwide to undertake community-level drying and storage to address post-harvest problems and take pro-active actions on price declines. Over the longer term, Cambodia needs sufficient stocks of dried nuts to support year-round domestic processing and stabilize prices for farmers.
Support Cashew federation and Association in Cambodia in providing price and market information during harvest seasons to help farmers manage risk more effectively.

Expand training for commune agriculture officers, focusing on planting, harvesting, storage and advisory skills. After training, commune officers should develop a plan of actions for a regular support of the cashew farmers in their communes. This approach was previously piloted by MAFF with support from the EU-German CAPSAFE project.

Mainstream the cashew sector into commune planning by educating and encouraging commune councils in cashew-growing areas to incorporate cashew promotion activities into the Commune Development Plan (CDP) and the Commune Investment Programme (CIP).

Mainstream the cashew sector into provincial investment plans, with a focus on high-potential provinces such as Kampong Thom, Kampong Cham, Kratie, Preah Vihear and Ratanakiri. Giving cashew explicit priority in provincial investment plans could help attract additional investment into the sector.
Continue training farmers on GAP, input and pest management, soil fertility management and climate adaptation, including irrigation techniques during drought.
Expand contract farming to strengthen linkages between farmers and processors.
Investment in processing: Because domestic processors still make only a limited contribution, achieving the 2027 and 2032 processing targets remains challenging. Attracting foreign investors is therefore a priority. Interested investors are awaiting the development of the Cashew Industrial Park in Kampong Thom and the approval of Qualified Investment Projects before commencing operations. Priority activities include:
Accelerate development of the Cashew Industrial Park in Kampong Thom to enable some processing factories to begin operations by early 2027.
Approve Qualified Investment Projects for cashew factories both inside the industrial park and in other high-potential provinces.
Link the Cashew Industrial Park with drying yards, storage warehouses, laboratories and by-product processing facilities.
Encourage the establishment of collection points or regional warehouses that act as market aggregators by drying, storing and supplying nuts for processing.
Study options for reducing production costs for cashew processing factories.

Create single window service inside the industrial park, modeled on Special Economic Zones, to facilitate customs procedures, SPS inspection, certificates of origin and other documentation while reducing private sector costs.
Allow Cambodian SME processors and exporters in the cashew sector to benefit from services and incentives available through the industrial park.
Expand technical training programs related to the cashew sector to support the industrialization agenda.
Working capital for processors: Year-round processing requires the purchase, drying and storage of large quantities of raw cashew nuts, but current bank products do not yet respond adequately to this seasonal financing need.

Based on the sector study, if output reaches 1 million tons, a target of 25 percent domestic processing would mean 250,000 tons. If processors require financing for only one third of that quantity, the required working capital would amount to around USD 100–120 million for stock purchases. Cambodia therefore needs new financial products. The government should also encourage private investment in cashew warehouses that can serve as market aggregators linking sellers and buyers.

Under the coordination of the National Bank of Cambodia and the Ministry of Economy and Finance, stakeholders could explore innovative and suitable financial products for the cashew sector. During interviews, processors and exporters referred to products similar to an overdraft facility aligned with the value chain and backed by guarantees from the Credit Guarantee Corporation of Cambodia (CGCC). the credit line, a revolving fund, would be linked to actual sale orders and would not require property as collateral.
Recommendations to strengthen the role of banks in addressing processor working-capital needs include:
Organize a consultation workshop on the role of banks in resolving processors’ working-capital constraints for reviewing banking experience and identifying suitable credit products.

Pilot procedures for a new financial product. The following example and ideas were raised during stakeholder interviews. Processors would receive prior approval from banks for an overdraft facility or credit line. During the harvest season, processors could use this credit to pay farmer cooperatives directly or through a new banking procedure. For the documents required by the bank, processors should provide sales contracts or purchase orders for processed cashew nuts, not for raw nuts. The Credit Guarantee Corporation of Cambodia could provide a guarantee for the loan in order to reduce bank risk.

Developing cashew warehouses is a strategic investment idea that could be combined with the Cashew Industrial Park. Such warehouses would create one or more market-aggregation hubs that buy raw cashew nuts from farmers in large volumes during harvest, dry and store them, and then supply domestic processors throughout the year or export them in bulk. The government could support this through subsidies or credit guarantees.
Recommendations to enable investors to help solve warehouse and raw material shortages for processors include:

Undertake an economic and business model study for cashew warehouses and use it to attract investors. This is consistent with Action 27 of the policy, which calls for mobilizing investors to build drying yards or dryers and storage facilities in strategic locations.
Attract investors to build cashew warehouses as strategic storage for the value chain.
Support projects for drying yards or dryers and warehouses through guarantees, subsidies or public-private partnership (PPP) arrangements.
Price competitiveness of processors: Domestic cashew processors face major cost pressures such as production costs, interest costs and limited labor productivity compared with competitor countries.
Key recommendations for reducing costs and increasing the price competitiveness of Cambodian cashew kernels include:

Convene meetings among senior leaders of key ministries to examine options for reducing costs in the cashew processing industry; especially within the Cashew Industrial Park; and consider support conditions similar to those available to the rice sector, thereby advancing the domestic processing goal.

Continue simplifying export procedures by studying the feasibility of a single window service for cashew exporters, allowing applications for all required documents such as electronic phytosanitary certificates, certificates of origin and customs documentation in a single place.
Continue improving transport infrastructure, including international ports and roads linking major cashew-producing provinces to ports.
Encourage small and medium-sized processors to install semi-automatic shelling machines to reduce costs and improve production techniques.
Develop capacity-building programs for owners and managers of cashew processing enterprises on production management, waste reduction, labor management and food standards.
Exports to key markets: Cambodian cashew nuts have reached many international markets, but export volumes remain small because exporters and processors still do not have sufficient capacity to capture market share and comply fully with importing country requirements. The MTR suggests that Cambodia should pay particular attention to target markets such as the European Union, the United States, China and ASEAN. Recommendations to strengthen exports include the following:
Develop specific export strategies for each major market, including the European Union, the United States, China and ASEAN.
Provide training and advisory support to exporters and processors to prepare them for export.

Build official data on the number of processors and exporters that hold certifications required by buyers. Some firms already hold HACCP and GMP certificates, but major markets often require BRC, IFS, FDA and similar standards, which enterprises must work toward step by step with appropriate support.
Support the operation of laboratories that serve export needs.

Organize peer-learning forums among processors and exporters on packaging and labeling, records of raw material flows, product coding, the drafting of standard operating procedures (SOPs) and production process, sales negotiation and contract preparation, pricing, international commercial terms (Incoterms), export standards, and digital trade.
Assign work plans to Cambodia's commercial representatives abroad to promote Cambodian cashew products.
Continue strengthening the reputation of Cambodian cashew products through geographical indications, certification marks and the collective mark as Cambodian Cashew.
Negotiate with China's General Administration of Customs (GACC) to ensure import procedures, phytosanitary protocols and other compliance requirements for the Chinese market.

Study logistics options for exports to suitable target markets, for example container shipping from Sihanoukville Port to Hainan Port in China. Moreover, land transport routes through Lao PDR or Viet Nam should also be examined.
Coordination and M&E: Implementation of the National Cashew Policy can become more effective through a stronger monitoring and evaluation system and more accountable stakeholder participation. Recommendations include:
Hold regular meetings among public institutions, the private sector, association and federation representatives, and development partners to discuss challenges and identify solutions.

Review and revise the indicators and performance measures for all 44 actions to ensure that they are linked to the three policy goals and respond more clearly to the needs of farmers, processors and exporters.

Strengthen the secretariat of the Inter-Ministerial Committee of the Implementation of the National Cashew Policy through training and the provision of resources for monitoring and evaluation. The secretariat should have the capacity to collect and verify data and to conduct policy research on key topics.
Expand outreach campaigns to cover benefit of the policy such as training, incentives and credit programs that directly benefit farmers and SMEs.

nextSteps: Prepare an action plan in response to the results of the mid-term review.
Review and revise the indicators and performance measures for all 44 strategic actions.
Convene high-level meetings to address critical issues such as the Cashew Industrial Park, Qualified Investment Projects, and working capital for processing.
Implement the monitoring and evaluation (M&E) plan.
mtr.method: Document review, 22 key informant interviews, visits to six processing factories in Kampong Thom and Kampong Cham, validation workshop. MTR rule: < 50% limited, ≥ 50% largely, completed = fully achieved.

actions.title: Disseminate new discoveries to farmers through the website of the Agricultural Information and Documentation Centre or on social media, setting up a platform where farmers can share their ideas and experiences.
actions.mtrSummary: New cashew cultivation techniques were compiled and disseminated through the website and video materials.

actions.title: Continue to conduct scientific research on cashew varieties, especially new varieties that are in line with Cambodia's ecosystem, climate / change, and target market needs.
actions.mtrSummary: Four high-yield varieties (M-23, M-10, IM-4, H-09) were released; the remaining varieties (M-1, IM-7, San-1) are still under trial.

actions.title: Implement the development and improvement of annual production measurement methods based on the latest available survey data - plantation yields; production costs; agro-input use; the investment level; the age of cashew trees; newly planted varieties; new plantings; and pests – in order to increase cashew production, as well as calculate production and identify potential for improvement.
actions.mtrSummary: A survey system for cashew yield and prices was created, and a cashew crop map was prepared.

actions.title: Prepare guidelines and disseminate to farmers and farm owners how to dry, grade, and store cashew nuts properly in accordance with technical conditions to ensure good quality and safety.
actions.mtrSummary: A manual on post-harvest techniques and cashew standards has been developed.

actions.title: Strengthen the implementation of existing regulations and assess environmental risks in the management of raw agricultural materials, especially pesticides, in order to optimise cashew productivity in accordance with technical standards.
actions.mtrSummary: Inspections have been conducted at 170 agro-input depots and relevant regulations have been disseminated and enforced.

actions.title: Increase productivity and protect the safety of farmers and farm workers through technical training, both theoretical and practical, to improve the quality of services, good agricultural practices and organic farming to be more accurate and effective in the cashew sector.
actions.mtrSummary: Thirteen farmer training courses on GAP have been delivered (against a target of 10).

actions.title: Recommend the establishment of a collective production group and a clear data collection study to identify the source of Cambodian cashew products in the market.
actions.mtrSummary: Four modern agricultural communities have been established (target: eight).

actions.title: Guide and coordinate the establishment of agricultural communities based on cashew crops and strengthen agricultural communities to function well.
actions.mtrSummary: Four modern agricultural communities have been established (target: eight).

actions.title: Coordinate the establishment of a Cashew Association and Federation.
actions.mtrSummary: Three associations have been officially registered: the Cashew Nut Association of Cambodia; the Prasat Balang Organic Cashew Farmers Association; and the Cambodia Cashew Federation.

actions.title: Strengthen farming contracts to ensure the supply chain by increasing value-added both during and post-harvest season through links between agricultural associations, farmer groups, and local processors for commercialisation in Cambodia.
actions.mtrSummary: Ninety-two contract-farming arrangements in cashew production have been implemented (target: 50).

actions.title: Strengthen the reputation of cashew products by improving the quality, taste, and the use of chemical inputs in accordance with technical standards in production.
actions.mtrSummary: Development is under way for 'Kampong Thom Cashew' as a geographical indication brand.

actions.title: Monitor and promote good agricultural practices / (CamGAP) and organic farming for cashew crops.
actions.mtrSummary: Thirteen GAP training courses were delivered, one farm was GAP-certified, and 398 hectares were certified as organic land.

actions.title: Create a budget package to mitigate the difficulties of farmers and processing plants in the event of natural disasters, epidemics, border closures, market disruptions, and flooding at harvest time.
actions.mtrSummary: ARDB's total credit portfolio reached approximately USD 53.96 million in support of the cashew value chain while SME Bank disbursed USD 3.2 million.

actions.title: Encourage banks and financial institutions to increase agricultural loan products or to adjust existing products to facilitate and lower interest rates.
actions.mtrSummary: The National Bank of Cambodia has supported risk-sharing arrangements (with CGCC) and issued related regulatory measures to facilitate and promote lending to the agricultural sector.

actions.title: Examine the possibility of constructing irrigation systems and other water sources to supply cashew crop production.
actions.mtrSummary: Water supply has been provided for plantations and mixed crops covering 756 hectares per year, however no meteorological or hydrological stations have been established to date.

actions.title: Prioritise demining plans to clear mines and unexploded ordnance for cashew plantations
actions.mtrSummary: A total of 4,662 hectares have been cleared of UXO for general cultivation.

actions.title: Include the cashew sector in strategic development plans and investment programs and cooperate with local communities and development partners to build and improve access roads to farms in accordance with the resources of subsidy fund collections.
actions.mtrSummary: Approximately 157 km of rural roads to cashew-producing areas have been improved (target: 460 km).

actions.title: Encourage the private sector to invest in processing cashew products for the domestic and export markets.
actions.mtrSummary: Three large cashew processing projects were approved.

actions.title: Encourage cashew processing factories to develop cashew processing capacity with the transfer of processing industry technologies for food production and cashew waste.
actions.mtrSummary: A total of four large-scale cashew processing factories and 40 micro, small, and medium (MSME) and artisanal cashew processing enterprises were registered.

actions.title: Study the economic benefits and encourage the private sector to establish cashew processing areas, which are located within cashew plantations or in industrial parks, in one location, in provinces that have potential for domestic supply. The establishment of such a processing / area could add great value to the rural economy.
actions.mtrSummary: Preparation of the Cashew Industrial Park in Kampong Thom is underway.

actions.title: Encourage the processing and management of cashew products for use as final products or semi- products to produce various final products.
actions.mtrSummary: Six training courses were organized on quality, safety, compliant processing techniques and waste management (target: 3).

actions.title: Provide technical advice about cashew processing plants to effectively manage waste, lower environmental impacts, and increase value-added from recycling cashew processing waste.
actions.mtrSummary: Technical advice was provided on waste management; six training sessions were delivered on quality, safety, compliant processing and waste management; the Ministry of Environment conducted 25 inspections of cashew and agro-industrial processing plants.

actions.title: Study and create standards related to cashew kernels, prepare procedures for recognising and implementing these standards according to the needs of importing countries. This would boost the quality and sustainability of Cambodian cashew processing by providing technical support and building capacity for processors so that they can obtain food standard certificates.
actions.mtrSummary: Revision of the national cashew kernel standard (CS 159:2015) is under way at the data-collection stage. / Documentation is being prepared for assessment under ISO/IEC 17065:2012.

actions.title: Guide and facilitate cashew processing enterprises and factories to enhance export productivity, ensure quality and food safety to a minimum level in accordance with the quality control system or standards, international food safety and management system, or equivalent systems certified by an accredited certification body.
actions.mtrSummary: Six training courses were delivered on quality, safety, compliant processing and waste management. / Documentation is being prepared for accreditation assessment under ISO/IEC 17065:2012.

actions.title: Examine the possibility of providing incentives through the exemption of, or reduction in, income tax, tax on processed cashew products, and value- added tax, to legal cashew operators who are able / to provide direct benefits to farmers.
actions.mtrSummary: Agricultural enterprises engaged in cashew-related business activities that applied for incentives under the four Prakas included: / Large enterprises: 5 enterprises / Small and medium enterprises: no enterprises submitted applications. /

actions.title: Examine the feasibility and provide the private sector with the necessary incentives to invest in, for instance, the construction of cashew warehouses at key strategic locations to store cashew products for year-round processing.
actions.mtrSummary: GDCE organized an outreach workshop on customs incentives for the Cashew Nut Association of Cambodia. / As of 31 January 2025, ARDB had a total credit portfolio of approximately USD 53.96 million, including USD 6 million invested in warehouse, silo and processing machinery.

actions.title: Mobilise investors to build drying yards and warehouses at key strategic locations for managing the harvest and the storage of cashew products for processing.
actions.mtrSummary: Drying yards currently exist mainly in Siem Reap and Kampong Thom provinces.

actions.title: Examine the possibility of facilitating a reduction in electricity prices for consumers in the cashew sector.
actions.mtrSummary: The electricity authority reviewed annual tariff schedules and granted a temporary three-month discount to processors in late 2023.

actions.title: Strengthen market information and data collection services for farmers and the public through various media so that they can monitor the market situation.
actions.mtrSummary: A publication on Cambodia's potential export products is being prepared / The Commerce Call Center (1266) was established / The Export Service Center was created / An Export Lab was set up.

actions.title: Facilitate the establishment of cashew trade associations or federations to gather together the private sector, exporters, processors and operators involved in the cashew business.
actions.mtrSummary: Support was provided to establish the Prasat Balang Organic Cashew Association, the Cashew Nut Association of Cambodia and the Cambodia Cashew Federation.

actions.title: Examine market trends, regional competition, and value-chains in order to promote the development of the cashew sector so that it is / consistent and inclusive.
actions.mtrSummary: Information on importing-country demand was disseminated for six markets - Korea, Japan, Malaysia, China, Singapore and Turkiye - in 2024, alongside trade representation in 16 countries.

actions.title: Continue to negotiate with export target countries about tariff exemptions or reductions, quotas, and trade facilitation, especially the effective implementation of the One Window Service Office (OWSO) mechanism.
actions.mtrSummary: The Cambodia-UAE Free Trade Agreement was signed, / Feasibility is being studied for trade MOUs or negotiations with Canada, Pakistan, Kazakhstan and others.

actions.title: Promote negotiations with target countries about facilitating the implementation of sanitary and phytosanitary rules, and build the capacity of Cambodian exporters and stakeholders to be able to comply with sanitation and phytosanitary standards. This can be achieved by encouraging and opening up the private sector to participate in the provision of sanitation and phytosanitary services.
actions.mtrSummary: Exports reached 30 countries including Belgium, China (including Taiwan), Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Thailand, the United Kingdom, Viet Nam, Bangladesh, Czech Republic, the Netherlands, the United States, the Philippines, Switzerland, France, Lao PDR, Saudi Arabia, Togo, the UAE, the Russian Federation, Turkiye, Australia, Israel, Malaysia, Myanmar, Singapore and Syria.

actions.title: Promote and disseminate information about the benefits of branding and packaging with quality and standards.
actions.mtrSummary: Regulatory and hygiene guidance on packaging was disseminated to all registered production and processing facilities registered with the Ministry of Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation (MISTI). / 12 trainings on packaging design and aesthetics and 16 workshops on promoting Khmer products were conducted.

actions.title: Promote and build a good branding reputation about products, using all means to widely disseminate this brand, to increase market competitiveness.
actions.mtrSummary: Support was provided for the development of collective brand; 'Cambodian Cashew'; and the geographical indication,'Kampong Thom Cashew. / High-quality Cambodian cashew products were showcased at trade fairs and trade missions both domestically and internationally. / 13 Cambodian private trade centers have been established overseas. / Khmer products were promoted through nine trade-attache activities.

actions.title: Facilitate the certificate provision mechanism for food product hygiene and strengthen the laboratory capacity in accordance with international standards. The operation of this laboratory may involve a public-private partnership.
actions.mtrSummary: Two certificates - GAP and HACCP - were granted to a small-scale cashew processing and packaging factory in Kampong Speu Province.

actions.title: Promote and facilitate the development of new digital technologies for electronic business operations.
actions.mtrSummary: Cooperation was provided with Alibaba / The Cambodiatrade.com platform was supported / Bakong system and cross-border QR payments were expanded.

actions.title: Develop new digital mechanisms and techniques to promote a well-recognised and confident marketing platform to sellers and buyers.
actions.mtrSummary: A digital platform for promoting raw cashew prices was developed and updated through the ministry's official website / Two training sessions on doing business in the digital era were delivered / MOUs were signed with private companies and retail marts to support market search.

actions.title: Organise a cashew business forum to promote Cambodia's cashew products and connect the private sector to international business networks.
actions.mtrSummary: Three domestic and four overseas business-matching forums were organized (three in China and one in Korea). / Four export promotion forums were organized targeting China, Viet Nam, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia / The Cashew and Pepper Trade Forum was introduced by MoC in 2025 as an annual event / Two MOU-signing events in the cashew sector were facilitated for the private sector.

actions.title: Launch a campaign about the use of local cashew products.
actions.mtrSummary: Six meetings were held to promote Cambodian cashews in supermarkets and retail marts / 17 workshops were held on identifying and promoting Cambodia's potential products / 22 companies participated in domestic and international trade fairs / Dedicated trade meetings on “Promoting the Export of Cambodia’s Potential Products to International Markets” were organized in conjunction with the 16th Cambodia Import-Export and One Province One Product Exhibition in 2023. / A trade meeting on “Developing Markets for Cambodia’s Potential Products”

actions.title: Promote and establish agro-tourism markets for cashew products on site.
actions.mtrSummary: Many cashew companies participated in Khmer product fairs linked to the River Festival, Sea Festival, National Ecotourism Day, and other domestic and international trade fairs.

actions.title: Continue to build the necessary physical infrastructure to connect factories, enterprises, and special economic zones to ports and export / gates.
actions.mtrSummary: The Phnom Penh–Sihanoukville Expressway has been completed 100%. / Construction of the Phnom Penh–Bavet Expressway has been officially launched. / A feasibility study is underway for the Phnom Penh–Siem Reap–Poipet expressway project (420 km). / The construction of the Funan Techo Canal has been officially launched. / The expansion of National Road No. 5 to four lanes has been completed. / The construction and full rehabilitation of National Road No. 10 is 98% complete. / The repair and maintenance project for National Road No. 4 is 73% complete. / The upgrading project for National Road No. 48 is 82% complete. / The upgrading, repair, and maintenance of Provincial Road No. 312 is 99% complete. / The construction of the Mekong River bridge in Kratie Province is 60% complete. / Eleven Diesel Multiple Unit (DMU) trains were procured from Japan. On the northern railway line, trains operate at speeds of 30–50 km/h, while on the southern railway line, they operate at speeds of up to 80 km/h. /

actions.title: Coordinate export procedures to reduce costs and increase the competitiveness of Cambodia’s cashew products.
actions.mtrSummary: The automated system for digital Certificates of Origin has been integrated into the National Single Window and connected to the ASEAN Single Window. / The Ministry of Commerce has delegated authority to 16 provincial Departments of Commerce in border provinces to issue digital Certificates of Origin. / The processing time to obtain phytosanitary certificates for cashew nut exports has been reduced to just three days. / The General Department of Agriculture under MAFF and the the General Department of Customs and Excise (GDCE) are working on an electronic Phyto system as part of the National Single Window / The General Department of Customs and Excise (GDCE) issued Letter No. 3611/24, dated 21 August 2024, regarding additional trade facilitation measures for agricultural exports. / Online systems have been implemented for registration applications and certification requests for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and handicraft businesses.

actions.title: Examine the possibility to reduce service fees, and to conduct the export process with speed and efficiency. The possibility of building standard warehouses for all agricultural products should also be explored.
actions.responsible: MPWT, MEF, Line Ministries, Provincial, MOC
actions.mtrSummary: Construction of a new container terminal in Sihanoukville Province (350 meters in length and 14.5 meters in depth) is underway and has reached 15% completion. / The Phnom Penh Autonomous Port has provided incentives for agricultural exports, including: (1) reduced container handling charges (lift-on/lift-off), (2) exemption from gate fees, and (3) an extension of container storage time at the yard from 7 days to 18 days. / Both autonomous ports have reduced container handling charges by USD 2 per container. / The General Department of Customs and Excise (GDCE) has finalized a draft Prakas and submitted Letter No. 1078/25 dated 7 March 2025 to the Ministry of Economy and Finance, requesting the exemption of scanner inspection fees for agricultural exports. A draft Prakas on this exemption has also been prepared. / The Ministry of Commerce has waived service fees for applications for Certificates of Origin in all forms for rice, small-scale handicraft products, and agricultural products. The maximum service delivery time is 16 working hours.
